links.comparator_used: Baseline alert rules before the 2021 PDSA review (2017 and 2019 data, with only ad hoc ICD-10 code changes)
links.outcome: Percentage of true positive CDS alerts and false positive alert count
links.effect: Median true positive alerts rose from 47.3% (combined 2017 and 2019 baseline) to 78.9%. Median false positives fell from 35 (IQR 12) to 15 (IQR 7) per month. Median true positives rose from 27 (IQR 9) in 2019 to 54 (IQR 11) per month in 2021-2022. The last four months of 2022 met the 85% goal. Total alerts were 71 (IQR 6) per month. PFO/small ASD alerts fell from 30 to 0 per month.
links.tradeoff: Adding the department code created a new source of false positives: patients seen in the congenital cardiology department without CHD, about 7 (IQR 4) alerts per month or half of all false positives. Duplicate alerts did not change (median 8 per month vs 9 and 12 at baseline). Review still took a median of 3 min per day. False negatives could not be reliably measured. The comparison was before-after, not randomized.
links.quote: Following the changes implemented in August 2021, there was a significant increase in true positive CDS, which has sustained, and the median of percent true positives increased to 78.9 %, an improvement from the baseline median of 47.3 %.

design_hint: iterative alert rule refinement (PDSA) to reduce false positive alerts
